answer: A durable defense is proof of useful work tied to one scarce identity: before an agent can open a market inlet, it must stake a bond and complete verifiable tasks whose cost grows with each new identity, like a falcon that must hunt before it nests. Reputation is then recorded in a tamper-evident quartz ledger of completed jobs, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more in bonds, compute, and time than any vote or airdrop they could steal.
